I only made that second post because people had asked for my time figures. for a couple reasons I was hesitant, but did it anyway. Then in that thread @BobBelcher asked about the times. So I ran some tests. These tests proved my first numbers wrong. Below I'll bore you w the details if you want to read all of that.

To cut to the chase- cue up the movie to the first frame. At 9:57:23 hit play. This will get you within a second or two of exactly midnight. The only way to get it exact is to test your copy on your HW. There are just too many variables for me to give it to you on a plate.

Remember this is theatrical release, anything else you're on your own.

I'm using the system clock for start time and checking midnight. I've set the system clock to https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/

My first set of numbers were based on the time code of VLC media player. I just took the numbers and did some math. Since then I've tested those numbers and it didn't work. So I got the numbers out of Windows Media Center (not Player) did the math and ran it again. Closer but still off. Somewhere in the player software it gives you wonky numbers. Idk but those hh:mm:ss numbers don't match real world time. So I did some more stuff and in the end had to time the fucker w a stopwatch app, a Movano wristwatch/chronograph(a stopwatch) and the system clock.

In real world time Hans Gruber eats pavement at 2:02:37 So a start time of 21:57:23 from first frame of the movie

On my reasoning for cueing the movie to the first frame.

I was trying to get some numbers that can be used by anyone regardless of the copy they have. I had my end point. I needed to define the beginning point to measure from. One common across all copies. Different copies, coming from different sources likely each have a different amount of leading 'tape'(that part w Co logos and shit). My DVD leader length is different than a copy downloaded and probably some other DVDs as well. So by starting at the first frame I eliminate that unknown and set a start common to every copy regardless of source.

In the end it depends on how exact the timing needs to be to satisfy you. i tried my best to get a start time that can be used by anyone and I think if you follow my instructions you'll get pretty close. If you want it exact or want/need to avoid the cueing thing, you'll have to crunch your own numbers. Sorry.
